races.title: State Assembly, District 29
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Robert Rivas
cands.bio: Democrat and 71st Speaker of the California Assembly, elected to the Assembly in 2018 and now representing District 29. Earlier he was a San Benito County supervisor (elected 2010, re-elected 2014), an adjunct professor at Gavilan College, a Monterey County senior board clerk, and a field representative for Assemblymember Anna Caballero.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), the California Teachers Association, SEIU Local 521, California Environmental Voters, Equality California and YIMBY Action.
His campaign site features endorsement quotes from Dolores Huerta, U.S. Rep. Zoe Lofgren, Santa Clara County District Attorney Jeff Rosen and Santa Clara County Supervisor Susan Ellenberg.

cands.gaps: Sources disagree on where he was born (Ballotpedia says both Hollister, California and Henderson, Nevada), so his birthplace is left out. We found no date for when he came to California. We found no sourced record of his actions or stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land purchases, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no documented statements from him on data centers. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys. We read only the campaign homepage and biography page, not its issue pages. We found no documented controversies in the pages we had.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site says he was raised in Paicines and attended school in San Juan Bautista and Hollister, but sources disagree on his birthplace, so the score uses the raised-here rule.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He has served in the Assembly since 2018 and has been Speaker since 2023. Before that he held two terms on the San Benito County Board of Supervisors, was a senior field representative for an Assemblymember, and was a Monterey County senior board clerk. He holds a Master's in Public Administration.
qual.why: He has prior legislative service and chamber leadership as Speaker, local elected office, legislative staff experience, and a public administration degree, which fits the high band for writing law and budgets.
qual.label: He has prior legislative service and chamber leadership as Speaker, local elected office, legislative staff experience, and a public administration degree, which fits the high band for writing law and budgets.

roots.summary: His campaign site says he was raised in Paicines and attended school in San Juan Bautista and Hollister, but sources disagree on his birthplace, so the score uses the raised-here rule.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: At his December 2024 swearing-in he said that "we must focus on building more housing and lowering energy costs," and called affordable housing "the civil rights struggle of our time."

cands.name: Dennis P. Sanchez
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 29 in 2026. Describes himself as a small business owner and regional manager with 30+ years of experience in construction and private security. Has not held elected office according to the pages reviewed.

endorsements.text: Listed as recommended in Elizabeth Barcohana's 'Lady with a Brain' voter guide (Sway voting group).

cands.gaps: His birthplace and the year he came to or began living on the Central Coast were not found. His work history (construction, private security, business ownership, regional manager) comes only from his campaign site, with no named employers or businesses and no independent confirmation. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. No news coverage, interviews or questionnaires were found. Nothing was found on his stance on data centers, development projects, homestead property taxes, foreign or institutional land buyers, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. No controversies or foreign ties were found.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site says he was raised in Castroville and is a lifelong Central Coast resident, but his birthplace is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Self-reported: more than 30 years in construction and private security, as a small business owner and regional manager; trained with the Salinas Police Department and was a Police Explorer Scout. No elected office or legislative or budget work found.
qual.why: Business owner and manager experience puts him in the middle band; no legislative, policy or budget record was found, and the work history comes only from his own campaign site.
qual.label: Business owner and manager experience puts him in the middle band; no legislative, policy or budget record was found, and the work history comes only from his own campaign site.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site lists public safety as a priority: 'Support law enforcement and safe communities.'

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign voter guide says he would vote Yes on Prop 45, which he describes as cutting red tape on housing projects by standardizing CEQA processes and timelines to reduce delays and costs.
